taxonomy_gate._note: Generic PARK-taxonomy gate for physical-park clusters (scripts/physical-park-taxonomy-gate.mjs). Clustering decides WHICH polygons form one physical object; this gate decides whether that object is a PARK. Row-level semantic signals: (a) park word in the NAME (word or compound ending, minus non-green compounds), (b) park token in the source LAYER field. The dataset-level scope ('parks AND green areas') never suffices alone. 2 row-level signals = PARK_CONFIRMED, 1 = PARK_LIKELY, 0 = TAXONOMY_AMBIGUOUS; a facility name without a park word = TAXONOMY_AMBIGUOUS; a non-park keyword (layer or name) without a park word = NON_PARK. PATH-LIKE geometry (linear AND narrow) downgrades one level. A cluster-level signal holds when >= member_signal_fraction of its members carry it. Path thresholds calibrated on the source's own labelled path layers (bicycle layers: mean width 3.3-6.2 m) vs the narrowest park-named coastal strip (10.3 m); linear = area/length^2 < linear_max_compactness (length >= 100x mean width).
taxonomy_gate._linear_single_signal_note: Added 2026-09-27 after the full PARK_LIKELY audit: Civil 2 ETAP #91 (layer-only evidence, 957 m x 8.2 m, compactness 0.0086) is one of two parallel verge bands around a road corridor whose twin #92 (5.7 m) was already path-like; the 8 m width cut was calibrated against a TWO-signal park strip and does not protect layer-only evidence. Linear threshold itself unchanged.
